title: Multi-hop and agentic RAG: when one search isn't enough
hook: Some questions need several searches that depend on each other's answers, not one lookup.
inPlainWords: When a question needs facts that depend on each other, one search pass can't find them all. The model needs to search, read what it found, and search again based on that.

useCase.title: "Can I return the gift my sister ordered, to my address?"
useCase.story: Answering needs the sister's order (a lookup by name), that order's return policy (depends on the product category), and whether returns can ship to a different address than the buyer's (a separate policy). No single search returns all three.

approaches.name: One search, one answer (standard RAG)
approaches.what: A single retrieval pass feeds the model once.
approaches.greatWhen: The question maps to one clear passage.
approaches.avoidWhen: The question needs facts that depend on each other.
approaches.example: Fails on the gift-return question because no single passage has all three facts.

approaches.name: Fixed multi-step pipeline
approaches.what: A hard-coded sequence of lookups: order, then category, then policy.
approaches.greatWhen: The question pattern is common and known in advance.
approaches.avoidWhen: The number or order of lookups varies by question.
approaches.example: A "gift return" flow hard-coded for this one case.

approaches.name: Agentic RAG: the model plans its own searches
approaches.what: The model decides what to search next based on what it's already found, looping until it has enough.
approaches.greatWhen: Question shapes vary and can't all be pre-coded.
approaches.avoidWhen: Latency and cost per question must stay low and predictable, or oversight of what it searches is hard to add.
approaches.example: The model searches the order, then the category, then the address policy, then answers.

approaches.name: Decompose the question first, then run standard RAG per part
approaches.what: Split the question into sub-questions up front, retrieve for each separately, then combine.
approaches.greatWhen: Sub-questions can be identified without needing earlier answers.
approaches.avoidWhen: Later searches truly depend on earlier results, as in this chain.
approaches.example: Works for independent sub-questions, but not this dependent one.

approaches.name: Cap the loop and log every step
approaches.what: Whichever method is used, bound the number of search rounds and record each one.
approaches.greatWhen: Always, with agentic or multi-step retrieval.
approaches.example: A 6-round cap with a full log of every search made.

challenge.question: Answering "Can I return my sister's gift to my address?" needs the order, then its category-specific return policy, then a separate address-change policy, each depending on the last. What approach fits?

options.text: Let the model plan and run each search based on what the previous one found, with a capped number of rounds and a log of each step
options.why: The searches genuinely depend on each other, which is exactly what agentic, bounded, logged retrieval is for.

options.text: One search pass over all documents
options.why: No single passage contains the order, category-specific policy and address policy together.

options.text: A fixed three-step pipeline hard-coded for this exact scenario
options.why: Works for this case but breaks the moment the question shape changes slightly.

options.text: Ask the customer to look up each fact themselves
options.why: Defeats the purpose of having an assistant.

bestCase.title: Bounded, logged, multi-step search
bestCase.example: The model looks up the order, reads the product category, searches the category's return policy, separately searches the address-change policy, then combines all three into one answer, in four logged search rounds.

worstCase.title: An unbounded loop
worstCase.example: The model keeps searching for a fact that doesn't exist in the library, running 40 rounds before timing out, and the customer waits a full minute for no answer.

route.travelling: Question: "Can I return my sister's gift to my address?"

steps.label: Look up the order
steps.goes: Finds the order under the sister's name.

steps.label: Search the address policy
steps.goes: Returns can ship to a different address with an ID match.

steps.label: Combine and answer
steps.goes: The bot explains both rules together, with citations.

steps.label: Cap and log
steps.goes: Every round is logged; a 6-round cap prevents endless loops.
steps.goesWrong: No cap is set, and a harder question sends the model into 40 rounds of fruitless search.

takeaway: When facts depend on each other, let the model search in rounds instead of once, but always cap the rounds and log every step.
